questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Kepler's second law, that a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time, follows directly from the conservation of:
questions.explanation: Gravity acts along the line joining the Sun and planet, so its torque about the Sun is zero and angular momentum stays constant, which is the law of areas.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1, so R = 1 Ω. In parallel the equivalent resistance is always smaller than the smallest resistor.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength associated with a particle of mass m moving with velocity v is given by:
questions.explanation: λ = h/p = h/mv, so heavier and faster particles have shorter wavelengths, which is why matter waves are noticeable only for electrons and lighter particles.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Among the isoelectronic species O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺, the largest ionic radius belongs to:
questions.explanation: All four have 10 electrons, so size depends on nuclear charge. Oxygen has the smallest nuclear charge of the set, so its ion holds the electrons most loosely and is largest.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a zero order reaction, the rate of reaction is:
options: Independent of the concentration of the reactant
Proportional to the square of concentration
questions.explanation: Rate = k[A]⁰ = k, so a plot of concentration against time is a straight line. Such kinetics is seen in some surface catalysed reactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol because:
options: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
Phenol has a higher molecular mass
Ethanol cannot lose a proton at all
questions.explanation: The negative charge of the phenoxide ion spreads over the ring by resonance, whereas the ethoxide ion has no such delocalisation and is destabilised by the +I effect of the alkyl group.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 7: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature treatment is called:
questions.explanation: Vernalisation prevents premature flowering and is needed by winter varieties of wheat, rye and some biennials such as cabbage.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Golden rice is a genetically modified crop enriched in:
questions.explanation: Golden rice accumulates beta carotene in the grain, which the body converts to vitamin A, so it was developed to fight vitamin A deficiency and childhood blindness.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A prolonged dietary deficiency of iodine in adults leads to:
questions.explanation: Without iodine the thyroid cannot make enough thyroxine, so the gland enlarges into a goitre and metabolic rate falls.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The blood vascular system of the cockroach is described as open because:
options: Blood flows entirely within closed vessels
Haemolymph flows freely through body sinuses bathing the organs
Its blood carries oxygen to every cell
questions.explanation: Colourless haemolymph pools in sinuses rather than staying in vessels, and it carries no respiratory pigment because tracheae deliver oxygen directly to the tissues.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 7: Structural Organisation in Animals
